classification.difficultyReason: Choose the appropriate prism or cylinder formula and invert it for a missing length, including a radius.

content.prompt: Find the missing length in each of these shapes.

spec.description: Shallow rectangular prism with long dimension x mm, depth 34 mm and thickness 13 mm. Top and two vertical faces are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Rectangular prism with mutually perpendicular dimensions x, 34 and 13 mm. Display model P(u,v,w) = (2.5u - 0.85v, 0.38u + 0.5v + 0.6w) for a unit box. Camera direction is proportional to (-0.228,-1,0.689), so faces u=0, v=0 and w=1 are visible. Hidden edges meet at (1,1,0). Projection lengths are not numerical measurements.

spec.description: Triangular prism with front base x cm, internal altitude 5 cm and prism length 8 cm. Rear cross-section is displaced upwards and left.
spec.mathematics: True cross-section has base x and altitude 5 cm; prism length is 8 cm. No triangle side length or angle is given. Display cross-section B=(0,0), C=(2,0), A=(1.3,1.6), with depth vector (-0.65,0.8). Faces are ABC, DEF, ABED, BCFE and CADF, where D,E,F are translated A,B,C. The viewing direction shows front triangle ABC and side ABED; the edges meeting at F are hidden. The vertical internal segment from A to BC represents the supplied altitude; no right-angle marker is added.
spec.answerVisibility: Base remains labelled x cm; no answer appears.

spec.description: Upright cylinder with a radial dimension x cm on its top and a height of 16 cm on the right.
spec.mathematics: Circular cylinder of radius x and height 16 cm. Orthographic projection of circular rims gives horizontal ellipses. Camera is above the cylinder; the top disk is visible, bottom rear semicircle hidden and bottom front semicircle visible. Vertical side boundaries are silhouettes.
spec.answerVisibility: The top arrow spans a radius, not a diameter; x remains unknown.
